title: Cohort activation heuristics and ops diary
body:
Purpose and scope
---
Notes: lightweight working log that captures heuristics we actually use when choosing micro-cohorts, the operational checklist for handoff, and a few quick simulation outcomes. Not a formal playbook — more of an ops diary + crib notes for stewards.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Prefer signal-constrained micro-cohorts: pick groups where one or two strong telemetry signals will show change fast (latency, rerate, user-reported failures).
- Reserve a 0.1%–1% random-exposed pilot for behavioral drift detection before any staged roll.
- Gate by latency and cost budgets first, then quality signals. If cost exceeds soft budget -> hold and throttle.
- Human gate every time we move beyond 5% cumulative exposure for novel model changes.

Guiding principles (short)
- Minimal surface area: smaller cohorts with higher signal-to-noise are better than broad but noisy ones.
- Orthogonality of risk: try to orthogonalize cohorts by device, region, and feature flags to help root cause.
- Single-change rule: only change one major variable per rollout wave (model variant / quant level / routing).
- Fast observability loops: ensure infra can surface the main signals in <10m for 99th percentile slices.

Heuristics for cohort selection (practical)
1) Feature-first cohorts
   - Choose cohorts tied to a product feature, not a business segment. Eg: users with "reply-drafts" enabled.
   - Rationale: easier to replay, synthetic traffic shaping possible, higher chance of fast signal.

2) Device/region orthogonality
   - If latency-sensitive change, pick mobile-only cohort in a single region (e.g., us-west1-mobile).
   - If safety change, pick desktop users + human-review channel.

3) Frequency buckets
   - Heavy users (top 5% by calls/day): good for throughput and cache behavior signals.
   - Medium users (5–50 calls/week): balance signal and privacy concerns.
   - Occasional users: low signal; avoid as primary cohort.

4) Behavioral proxies (quick list)
   - Users who trigger rerank/clarify flows often -> good for quality signals.
   - High rate of short-concat prompts -> sensitive to context-window regressions.

Activation ladder (conservative sequence)
- seed 0.1% synthetic traffic (canary-run) -> 0.1% real random users -> 0.5% microcohort by feature -> 2% targeted cohorts -> 10% broader cohort (if all green)
- Wait windows: 30m after each jump for latency/cost; 24h for quality/behavioral signals for medium-risk changes.

Handoff checklist for release steward (quick)
- [ ] Slack announcement: #release-orchestra + @oncall (template link in Confluence).
- [ ] Attach test prompts & golden responses (PR/branch id).
- [ ] Confirm telemetry dashboards: latency, token-cost, rerank delta, safety-classifier rate.
- [ ] Synthetic traffic plan ready (names of scripts + load profile).
- [ ] Rollback plan exists & smoke test route available.
- [ ] Human-review queue and rotas assigned if safety gating enabled.

Signal taxonomy and weight hints (ops-friendly)
- Tier A (immediate guardrail): p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, GPU OOM, infra errors. (auto-block 3x baseline)
- Tier B (quality): rerank delta, hallucination proxy (classifier hits), user corrections. (manual review threshold: >15% change)
- Tier C (business-looking): retention proxies, user-satisfaction surveys. (longer window)

Fallback and hybrid routing notes
- Soft fallback routing: route 100% of requests to primary variant but attach a sampled duplicate to new variant for scoring. Use this for read-only quality assessment.
- Dual-write telemetry: ensure new variant writes logs to the same observability stream (tagged) — otherwise comparisons are noisy.

Operator runbook snippets (copy these into pager bot)
- Immediate action if p95 latency > baseline * 2 for 15m: scale pool + throttle heavy-user cohorts + mute rollout.
- If safety classifier spike > 3x baseline and human-review backlog grows > 5x: pause rollout, escalate to safety-lead.
- Cost overshoot: if token-cost per request > expected * 1.5 for 1h, throttle non-critical traffic (batching tweaks), notify finance contact.

Synthetic traffic and replay strategy (practical notes)
- Two-tier synthetic traffic: low-fidelity hammer scripts for latency/capacity, and high-fidelity conversational replays for quality.
- Use anonymized historical traces for replays (day-of-week and hour matching).
- Warm KV/prefix caches before stepping real traffic to avoid cold-start artifacts.

Quick simulation results (from local sim run on 2025-11-18)
- Scenario A: model v3 (batching optimized) vs v2 -> 25% lower p50 latency for heavy users, but 8% increase in hallucination classifier hits on clarifying prompts.
- Scenario B: quantized variant -> cost -42% token-GPU but p95 latency +18% in mobile region due to kernel mismatch.
- Action: hold quantized on mobile cohorts; proceed with v3 in server-side cohorts with human gates.

Communications templates (one-liners)
- Pre-rollout (to stakeholders): "Planned small-batch activation tomorrow 09:00 UTC for feature X. Main guards: latency, safety-classifier. Oncall: @infra-oncall. Link: <dashboard>."
- Post-step update: "Stepped to 0.5% microcohort. Latency p95 +6% (within soft threshold). Safety classifier steady. Proceed? (yes/no)"

Unresolved questions / TODOs
- We still lack a short-run user-correction metric that's reliable within 6h; consider instrumenting an explicit "correction button" on beta cohorts.
- Need a lightweight synthetic traffic harness that can reproduce prefix-caching behavior cheaply. (TODO: @Ethan to prototype)
- Confirm retention of per-token cost telemetry downsampled at 1s granularity; current dashboards are 1m and hide bursts.

Notes-to-self (stream-of-consciousness)
- keep human gates simple: names + two approvers. Avoid multi-committee for early steps.
- avoid mixing routing + quantization in same rollout wave — learnings get confounded.

Appendix: quick checklist (single page view)
- Pre: run sim, attach golden prompts, set dashboards, announce slack, synthetic traffic ready.
- Step: warm caches -> step -> observe 30m for infra, 24h for quality -> escalate if any Tier A or B threshold breached.
- Post: capture signal deltas, tag commit, update rollout ledger, schedule retro if any signal tripped.

Links and refs
- Runbook skeleton: confluence://rollouts/activation-canvas
- Simulation repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim
- Pager templates: confluence://ops/pager-templates

Recent edits (journal)
- 2025-11-20 initial draft, heuristics and sketch of activation ladder.
- 2025-11-25 added synthetic traffic plan and operator runbook snippets (Ethan).
- 2025-12-05 appended local sim outcomes and tightened handoff checklist (Priya).

End of doc.
